12.t: Working with data: a tug of war
q: In which rounds were the forces balanced?
Calculate the resultant force in round 2.
The rope stayed still in round 4, though both teams pulled harder than in round 1. Explain.
The forces are balanced again (1500 = 1500): the resultant is zero, so there is no change in motion.
In round 3 the rope was moving at a steady speed while the forces were 1150 and 1400 N. Is this possible? Explain.
Not if those were the only forces: a 250 N resultant would accelerate it. Steady speed needs balanced forces, so there must be another force (e.g. friction on the ground) or the readings are wrong.
